egg-salad-sandwich-on-white.title: Egg Salad Sandwich on White Bread

content.title: About
content.content: The egg salad sandwich on white bread is a classic light snack consisting of soft white bread generously spread with egg salad made from boiled eggs, mayonnaise, mustard, and seasonings. It’s perfect for breakfast, lunch, or a picnic.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg salad became popular in the United States in the early 1920s and quickly spread to diners and cafeterias.
The traditional recipe uses hard‑boiled eggs, but some variations add finely chopped pickles or green onions.
White bread for this sandwich is often lightly toasted to add a subtle crunch.
The sandwich is commonly cut into triangular halves for easy handheld eating.
In some regions a pinch of turmeric is mixed into the mayo, giving the salad a golden hue.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs provide a high‑quality complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Egg salad supplies vitamin B12, riboflavin, and folate, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Mayonnaise made with vegetable oils adds monounsaturated fats that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Eggs contain lutein and zeaxanthin, antioxidants that help maintain healthy vision.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat provides lasting fullness.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to eggs may experience reactions ranging from mild to anaphylaxis when consuming the sandwich.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Mayonnaise and bread add significant calories; portion control is advisable for weight management.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Eggs must be fully cooked and kept refrigerated to prevent salmonella contamination.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with elevated cholesterol levels should consume in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is easy to eat by hand, typically sliced into triangles. Add lettuce, tomato, or avocado for extra freshness and flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the assembled sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage keep the components separate: bread in a dry place and egg salad chilled.

content.title: About
content.content: Raw mangoes are the ripe fruits of the mango tree (Mangifera indica), native to tropical regions of Asia, Africa, and South America. They have a sweet, fragrant flavor, juicy flesh, and a thin, slightly fibrous skin.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mango is called the "king of fruits" in India.
There are over 400 mango varieties, differing in taste, color, and size.
Ancient cultures used mango in rituals and as a symbol of prosperity.
Mango seeds are rich in oil, used in cosmetics and cooking.
India harvests more than 20 million tons of mangoes each year.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Mango provides a high amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene in mango converts to vitamin A, essential for vision and skin health.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Beneficial antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols in mango help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Potassium and magnesium in mango contribute to normal blood pressure.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to mango, especially those sensitive to urushiol in the skin.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Raw mangoes are high in natural sugars, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improperly stored mangoes can harbor bacteria that cause food poisoning.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw mango can be eaten on its own, sliced into salads, smoothies, desserts, or used in sauces. The skin is usually peeled with a knife or peeler, and the flesh is cut into cubes or strips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep unripe mangoes at room temperature until they ripen, then transfer to the refrigerator where they stay fresh for up to 5 days. Avoid airtight containers to prevent moisture buildup.

content.title: About
content.content: Margarita mix is a ready-to-use non‑alcoholic blend for making a classic margarita. It contains lime juice, flavorings, a sweetener and a pinch of salt, reproducing the taste of the traditional cocktail without alcohol.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Margarita mix is popular in mocktail bars as a convenient alternative to the alcoholic version.
The formula often uses lime concentrate instead of fresh juice for consistent flavor.
Low‑calorie versions are available, allowing control over sugar intake.
The mix stays fresh in the refrigerator for up to 6 months after opening.
In some markets the mix is sold as a powder that is reconstituted with water.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Lime juice provides vitamin C, which supports the immune system.

items.title: No alcohol
items.content: Absence of ethanol makes the drink safe for children and those avoiding alcohol.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The water base helps maintain proper hydration.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Lime contains flavonoids with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: The acidity of lime can promote healthy digestion.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: People allergic to citrus may experience reactions.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some formulations contain added sugar, which may be unsuitable for diabetics.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Preservatives used for shelf‑life may not be acceptable to all consumers.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can irritate sensitive teeth or stomach.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Mix 30–40 ml of the mix with 150–200 ml of cold still or sparkling water, add ice and garnish with a lime wedge. It can also be used in mocktails, smoothies, or as a base for marinades.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated after opening and seal tightly. Typical shelf life after opening is 1–2 months, but follow the manufacturer’s guidelines.
